entry.title: ’Battery and Hydrogen Technology’ at TU Braunschweig

media:group.media:title: ’Battery and Hydrogen Technology’ at TU Braunschweig
media:group.media:description:
What will tomorrow’s energy supply look like? 🔋💧
Modern society relies on sustainable power supply. It became a necessity in order to maintain our standard of living, our economy, as well as our safety and well-being. The transition from fossil to renewable energy opens up opportunities to new technologies, that can ensure this need. This forms the core of both the Bachelor's and Master's programmes in Battery and Hydrogen Technology at TU Braunschweig.
The Bachelor’s programme in ’Batterie- und Wasserstofftechnologie’ and the Master’s programme in ‘Battery and Hydrogen Technology’ combine theory and practice in a unique way:
⚡ Hands-on projects right from the start 🌍 Collaboration in international teams 🏭 Early contact with industry
This way, you’ll gain valuable experience for your future whilst you’re still studying.
➡️ Bachelor’s info: www.tu-braunschweig.de/bwt ➡️ Master’s info: www.tu-braunschweig.de/bht
Be a part of the energy transition and make your contribution as an engineer in creating a sustainable and climate friendly future. 🚀
The video was produced in collaboration with @dieregionbraunschweigwolfsburg as part of the regional marketing campaign for the Braunschweig-Wolfsburg region.

media:group.media:title: Bioentrepreneurship studieren in Braunschweig
media:group.media:description:
Wie kommt Forschung eigentlich in die echte Welt? Und wie wird aus einer Idee ein Bio-Start-up? Der neue Master Vertiefungsrichtung Bioentrepreneurship an der Technischen Universität Braunschweig in Kooperation mit dem Helmholtz-Zentrum für Infektionsforschung verbindet Life Sciences mit Start-up-Mindset.
Im Video teilen Bio-Start-up-Gründer:innen ihre Stories – ehrlich, direkt und aus der Praxis: Wie sie gestartet sind, was sie gelernt haben und warum sie sich so ein Studium damals gewünscht hätten.
Was dich erwartet: Bio ❤ Business = Bioentrepreneurship Von der Forschungsidee → zur echten Anwendung → bis hin zur möglichen Kommerzialisierung.
Du lernst, wie man Wissenschaft in Lösungen übersetzt, unternehmerisch denkt und wie Bio-Start-ups und Innovationen wirklich entstehen. In Deutschland einzigartig – und nur an der Technischen Universität Braunschweig!
Quick Facts: • Start: WiSe 2026/27 • Für Bachelor-Absolvent:innen aus Life Sciences oder Business • Entwickelt mit dem Braunschweiger Start-up-Ökosystem
► Mehr Informationen: https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/bioentrepreneurship und https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/studienangebot/bioentrepreneurship-schwerpunkt-in-den-masterstudiengaengen-biotechnologie-und-technologie-orientiertes-management

media:group.media:title: Personal experiences video: Beyond the Data – Memories from the tropical forests
media:group.media:description:
🌿 Science is not only about samples, measurements, and results. It is also about the people, places, and experiences behind the research.
🎥 In this FORVEST-Hg project video, researchers share their personal experiences from fieldwork in tropical forests. What was the most challenging part? How did the local spirit of “Pura Vida” become part of the journey?

Researchers from the FORVEST-Hg project give personal insights into the challenges, emotions, and moments that made this field campaign unique.

entry.title: Breathing Mercury: The role of tropic forests in the global mercury cycle

media:group.media:title: Breathing Mercury: The role of tropic forests in the global mercury cycle
media:group.media:description:
🌳 Did you know that tropical forests act as a “green lung” for more than just CO2? They also capture mercury — a highly toxic pollutant that circulates globally through the atmosphere.
🌍 This is where the international project FORVEST-Hg comes in. Researchers from the Institute of Geoecology at TU Braunschweig study how tropical forests influence the global mercury cycle.
💡 The team travelled to tropical dry forests and rainforests in Costa Rica. Their goal? To understand how trees capture mercury from the air and store it in leaves, litter, wood, and soils.
🔬 This research also provides insights into how vulnerable tropical forests and their mercury dynamics are to longer dry periods under climate change.
Dr. Marta Pérez-Rodríguez, Dr. Juan F. Morales Arteaga, and Prof. Harald Biester from the Institute of Geoecology, TU Braunschweig, give an insight into the project, the sampling process, and their preliminary findings.
Credits: Filming and editing by Markus Bauriedl (+43 699 11202825) Photo and video material: FORVEST-Hg team / TU Braunschweig.
#mercury #tropicalforests #FORVESTHg #tubraunschweig #environmentalscience

entry.title: Kinder-Uni 2025: Recycling – Warum werden alte Batterien recycelt?

media:group.media:title: Kinder-Uni 2025: Recycling – Warum werden alte Batterien recycelt?
media:group.media:description:
Die Kinder-Uni Braunschweig ist eine Veranstaltung für Kinder zwischen 8 und 12 Jahren. In spannenden Vorlesungen könnt ihr auf unterhaltsame Weise Wissenschaft entdecken und mehr über verschiedene Themengebiete erfahren. Die Vorlesungen sind kostenfrei und bieten die Möglichkeit, von echten Forschenden zu lernen und ihnen Fragen zu stellen!
Am 22. November 2025 erklärte Prof. Arno Kwade den Junior-Studierenden, warum alte Batterien recycelt werden.
Stell dir vor, wir verbrauchen für den Bau von Batterien dauerhaft wertvolle Rohstoffe. Rohstoffe sind Materialien aus der Natur, die von Menschen weiterverarbeitet werden, um daraus Produkte herzustellen, die wir täglich benutzen. Bauen wir zum Beispiel ganz viele E-Autos, dann hätten wir in 20 bis 30 Jahren diese Rohstoffe fast komplett verbraucht. Damit das nicht passiert, müssen wir die gebrauchten Batterien recyceln und aus den gewonnenen Materialien wieder neue Batterien bauen. Ziel ist es, in fünf Jahren 95 Prozent der Metalle aus alten Batterien zurückzugewinnen.
Welche Schritte sind notwendig, um aus alten Batterien neue Materialien zu gewinnen? Was können wir tun, damit möglichst alle Batterien recycelt werden? Diese und weitere spannende Fragen wurden in der Vorlesung beantwortet.

English version:
Kinder-Uni Braunschweig 2025: Recycling – Why are old batteries recycled?
The Kinder-Uni Braunschweig is an event for children between the ages of 8 and 12. In exciting lectures, you can discover science in an entertaining way and learn more about various topics. The lectures are free and offer the opportunity to learn from real researchers and ask them questions!
On November 22, 2025, Prof. Arno Kwade explained to our junior students why old batteries need to be recycled.
Imagine that we continually consume valuable raw materials for the construction of batteries. Raw materials are materials from nature that are further processed by humans in order to make things we use every day. If we build many electric cars, we would have almost completely used up these raw materials in the next 20 to 30 years. To prevent that from happening, we must recycle the used batteries and build new batteries from the recovered materials. The goal is to recover 95 % of the metals from old batteries within five years.
Which steps are necessary to extract new materials from old batteries? What can we do so that as many batteries as possible are recycled? These and other exciting questions were answered in the lecture.
► Further information about the Kinder-Uni Braunschweig can be found on our website: https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/en/transferservice/knowledge-transfer/kinderuni
